jobs.title: Drift Wood #21 · the envelope
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: An envelope from Portland arrives in the background. Nobody in the strip mentions it. Panel 1: a teenage boy's bedroom with a drawing table by the window, an envelope propped against a lamp on the dresser in the background, a mother's hand setting down a plate of toast, black and white (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "I'm working.". Mother says, in a small balloon, "It's toast, Arthur.". Panel 2: close-up of a pen drawing a cartoon cashier on bristol, an unopened envelope soft in the background. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teenage boy eating toast with one hand and drawing with the other, an envelope still propped on the dresser behind him (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Cashiers are the Greek chorus of this town. They see everyone and comment on nothing.". Panel 4: a teenage boy asleep on his arms at a drawing table at night, a desk lamp's cone of light falling on an unopened envelope propped against it, black and white, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
